current.text: He is the clear sixth man for OKC. The projected starting guards are Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Cason Wallace, and the only open question in the starting five is whether Mitchell starts over Wallace.
Most experts expect Wallace to keep the starting job over Mitchell.
He should still play close to starter minutes off the bench and get spot starts.
OKC traded away Lu Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe to save money, which leaves more guard and wing minutes and usage for Mitchell.
If Gilgeous-Alexander, Wallace or Jalen Williams miss games, he would start and play about 31 minutes. His value would soar if Gilgeous-Alexander gets hurt.
His best fantasy games last season came while key teammates were out. His efficiency and usage dropped as they returned, and he ranked 189th over the last three months of the season.
Experts warn that his numbers from last season overstate his value with a healthy roster around him.
His preseason has been a little down.

Experts disagree on his price. One calls him a late swing pick with more upside than Wallace and says his ESPN rank of 243 is far too low. Others say his value is overblown and that he is a late flyer at most.
Ryland expects him to share the floor more with the top players this season, which should make him more efficient. He sees Gilgeous-Alexander, Jalen Williams and Mitchell together as the best lineup.
He is extension eligible next summer.
OKC has a league-minimum 13 back-to-backs, and its schedule is good with our March 28 end date.
OKC is projected to win about 57 to 62 games and be a top two seed in the West.

durable.text: His fantasy profile is thin. He has good FG% and FT%, but no standout category. His scoring, rebounds, assists and blocks are modest.
He takes few threes. Under 30% of his shots come from three.

He shoots better next to the stars because they create open looks for him. Off the bench he is the lone creator and takes tough shots such as pull-up threes, hard mid-range jumpers and physical drives. Last season he shot 42% from three in 16 starts and 32% in 41 games off the bench.
He has played two NBA seasons and has not had a healthy one yet.

note: He is a borderline pick in our 144-player draft. Yahoo ranks him 128th at an average cost of 1.0 USD, ESPN ranks him 243rd at 0.4 USD, and nobody drafted him in our league last season. He is worth a 1 USD final-round bid for his strong FT% (86%) and steals, and as a handcuff to Gilgeous-Alexander and Jalen Williams. He fits any build but has no standout category. Early in the season, check whether he starts over Wallace and gets close to 30 minutes with the stars healthy. If he does not, he can go back to waivers.
